checks.note: Exactly three days (Day 1–3), each with a morning-to-night plan.
Each day has named food stops at breakfast, lunch and dinner, plus market grazing and pastry or bagel crawls. Only the afternoon sightseeing blocks have no food.

The plan is mostly mid-range: Schwartz's, bagels, markets, Mastard and BYOB tips. Pricey spots like Au Pied de Cochon and Joe Beef are marked as splurges and come with cheaper alternatives. A daily estimate of about CAD 260–400 fits a mid budget.
Covers October weather (8–14°C, layers, rain jacket), Mont Royal fall colors, October produce at Jean-Talon (apples, squash, cider) and the Botanical Garden's autumn lantern festival.

Nearly every stop is a specific real place (Olive et Gourmando, Schwartz's, St-Viateur, Fairmount, Jean-Talon, Damas, La Banquise, Joe Beef, Qing Hua). Minor accuracy problems: 'Régiliza' doesn't match any Montreal restaurant I know and may be made up. Satay Brothers is in Saint-Henri near Atwater, not 'the Village'.

unasked_content: Satay Brothers is placed in 'the Village/Atwater area'. It is actually in Saint-Henri, so the Village part could send the traveler to the wrong neighborhood.
'Régiliza' is offered as a dinner pick but may not be a real restaurant, which would waste a dinner slot.
Lodging is listed at CAD 150–220 per person per day, which looks like a per-room price labeled per person. This could inflate the budget for travelers sharing a room.
